questiontext.text:
The exercise above checks five values of \(a\). Remainders prove a statement like it for every integer at once.

Statement: for every integer \(a\), \(a^2 + {@cc@}\) is not divisible by {@md@}.

Write \(a = {@md*k@} + r\), where \(k\) is an integer and \(r\) is one of \(0, 1, \ldots, {@md-1@}\). Expanding shows that \(a^2 + {@cc@}\) leaves the same remainder on division by {@md@} as \(r^2 + {@cc@}\).

Enter the remainders of \(a^2 + {@cc@}\) on division by {@md@} for \(r = 0, 1, \ldots, {@md-1@}\), as a list in that order. Type a list in square brackets, for example [5, 6, 7].

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Every integer \(a\) leaves one of the remainders \(0, 1, \ldots, {@md-1@}\) on division by {@md@}, so there are {@md@} cases, \(a = {@md*k@} + r\). In each case \[({@md*k@} + r)^2 + {@cc@} = {@md@}\left({@md*k^2@} + 2kr\right) + r^2 + {@cc@},\] and the first term is a multiple of {@md@}, so the remainder of \(a^2 + {@cc@}\) depends only on \(r\).

[[foreach row="rtable"]] [[/foreach]]
\(r\)\(r^2 + {@cc@}\)remainder on division by {@md@}
{@row[1]@}{@row[2]@}{@row[3]@}

So the list is {@ta1@}. No remainder is 0, so \(a^2 + {@cc@}\) is never divisible by {@md@}. These {@md@} cases prove the statement for every integer, which no list of values could do.[[if test="is(md = 3)"]] The exercise's values fit: \(a = 6\) and \(a = 9\) leave remainder 0, so \(a^2 + 1\) leaves 1; \(a = 7\) and \(a = 10\) leave 1, giving 2; \(a = 8\) leaves 2, giving 2.[[/if]]

questiondescription.text: This question is adapted from Exercise 5, p. 22, in Section 5 of Bokhove, C., Thoma, A., Gammack, D., Yu, L. H. S., Roberts, S. and Downey, F., Thinking about Proof, 1st edition, University of Southampton, 2022: the check of five values is replaced by remainder cases that cover every integer, with the modulus and the constant varied.

feedbackvariables.text: /* True when every entry differs from the correct remainder by a multiple of md: right values, not (all) reduced. */ congr: every(lambda([uu], is(mod(uu, md) = 0)), ans1 - ta1);

node.description: Diagnostic: right values, but not all reduced to remainders (includes dunred)

truefeedback.text: The numbers in your list come from the right calculation, but they are not all remainders. A remainder on division by {@md@} is one of \(0, 1, \ldots, {@md-1@}\): for example, {@3*md + 1@} leaves remainder 1, because \({@3*md + 1@} = 3 \times {@md@} + 1\). Replace each number in your list by its remainder.
These are the remainders of \(r^2\). Add {@cc@} before finding each remainder.

falsefeedback.text: For each \(r\) from 0 to {@md-1@}, work out \(r^2 + {@cc@}\) and its remainder on division by {@md@}. For example, \(r = 2\) gives \(2^2 + {@cc@} = {@4 + cc@}\).
